meta.title: Nyquist plot generator with encirclement counting
meta.tools: Contour mapping of L(jω), numerical winding number (argument principle), Routh–Hurwitz for the prediction, closed-loop pole computation
meta.summary: Map the imaginary axis through L(s) = K/((s+1)(s+2)(s+3)), count encirclements of −1 with a winding-number algorithm, and find the gain at which the closed loop goes unstable — predicted beforehand with the Routh–Hurwitz criterion.
meta.problem: Nyquist's criterion turns a question about roots into a question about a curve. Can a program count the encirclements reliably?
meta.theory:
Argument principle: as s traverses the Nyquist contour, 1+L(s) winds around 0 (equivalently L around −1) N = Z − P times, Z = closed-loop RHP poles, P = open-loop RHP poles
(here 0). Characteristic polynomial $s^3+6s^2+11s+6+K$: Routh gives stability for 6·11 > 6+K, i.e. **K < 60**; at K = 60 the loop crosses −1 at ω = √11 = 3.317 rad/s.
meta.method:
L(jω) on ω ∈ [−10⁴, 10⁴] (log-dense near 0) plus the vanishing arc; winding number = total change of arg(1+L)/2π, computed from unwrapped phase. K swept 1–200; closed-loop
poles from numpy.roots for comparison; critical K and crossing frequency by bisection on the winding count.
